title: Wigwame Swamp (Cold Spring Harbor)
summary: Wigwame, or Wigwam, is recorded as a swamp in Huntington town. A local note places the early "wigwam swamp" where the main part of Cold Spring Harbor village now stands.
history_content: Early Huntington records connect the name with a highway laid out from the head of the swamp. Later place-name summaries continued to associate Wigwame Swamp with Cold Spring Harbor.
translation_content:
The name belongs to the wider Algonquian wigwam word family for a dwelling or home. Related forms carry meanings such as "in his house" or "in their house."

Why Place Names Matter

“Why should we be concerned about place names? These names are a basic way in which we gain meaning about the surrounding landscape. We all use place names to mark our travels through everyday life, but we seldom acknowledge the stories enmeshed within these names.”

— National Park Service, Place Names Along the Santa Fe National Historic Trail (2025), opening paragraph; page last updated April 23, 2025
preservation_content: Wigwame Swamp preserves an Indigenous-language place-name within the later built village landscape of Cold Spring Harbor. The modern map point is approximate and intended to make the placename visible for review.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in the main village area of Cold Spring Harbor, based on the source note locating the swamp there. Coordinates are approximate and not exact historic coordinates.
